prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Disclosed is a bottle trap having a main body having an open end coupled to a tailpiece pipe and a tapered closed end having at least one face inclined at a first angle with respect to axis of the main body. The bottle trap also includes a cylindrical trap element received on the open end and extending axially into the main body up to at least half the length of the main body. An outlet orifice is configured on peripheral surface of the main body perpendicularly thereto. The outlet orifice is adapted to be coupled to a horizontal drain pipe. Also, a thread-less coupling is configured at the open end and outlet orifice, respectively, for connecting the tailpiece pipe and the drain pipe, respectively, thereto for ensuring a leak-proof coupling. Moreover, at least one sealable drain orifice is configured at the at least one inclined face of the tapered closed end.

outputs.L3:
The bottle trap comprises a main body having an open end connected to a tailpiece pipe and a tapered, closed end that includes at least one inclined face. A cylindrical trap element extends axially from the open end into the main body for at least half of the body’s length.

An outlet orifice is formed in the peripheral surface of the main body and is oriented substantially perpendicular to the body’s longitudinal axis. The outlet orifice connects the bottle trap to a generally horizontal drain pipe. Threadless couplings at both the open end and the outlet orifice provide secure, leak-proof connections to the tailpiece pipe and the drain pipe, respectively.

To facilitate drainage, cleaning, or maintenance, at least one sealable drain orifice is provided on an inclined face of the tapered closed end.
outputs.L4:
A bottle trap for use in a plumbing drainage system includes an elongated, generally cylindrical trap element configured to retain a quantity of water and thereby form a barrier against the passage of sewer gases. The trap element has a closed lower end that tapers toward a drain portion. An inclined drain face is formed at the tapered end and contains a drain orifice through which accumulated water, sediment, and debris can be discharged. The drain orifice is normally closed by a removable, fluid-tight plug or other sealing member, allowing the trap to be emptied and cleaned without dismantling the complete assembly.

An inlet at the upper portion of the trap element receives a substantially vertical tailpiece extending from a sink, basin, or similar plumbing fixture. A substantially perpendicular outlet extends laterally from the trap element and connects to a generally horizontal drain pipe. The relative arrangement of the inlet and outlet directs wastewater through the trap while maintaining the standing-water seal required for normal operation.

The tailpiece and drain pipe are attached by threadless couplings. Each coupling may include a compression sleeve, gasket, O-ring, or comparable sealing component that engages the exterior surface of the associated pipe. A retaining collar or housing holds the sealing component in place and provides a secure, leak-resistant connection without requiring threaded pipe ends. This construction simplifies installation, permits limited positional adjustment, and reduces the risk of leakage caused by damaged, misaligned, or improperly tightened threads.

During use, wastewater enters through the tailpiece, passes into the cylindrical trap element, and exits through the perpendicular outlet into the horizontal drain line. A portion of the water remains in the lower region of the trap element to establish the gas-blocking seal. When maintenance is required, the plug in the inclined drain face can be removed so that the retained water and collected material flow through the drain orifice. The tapered lower end and inclined face guide the contents toward the opening, promoting more complete drainage and easier removal of debris.

The resulting bottle-trap assembly provides compact construction, reliable leak-proof pipe connections, and convenient access for draining and maintenance. Because the trap can be emptied through the sealable drain orifice, routine servicing may be performed without disconnecting the inlet or outlet pipes, reducing labor and minimizing disturbance to the surrounding plumbing installation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a bottle trap featuring a tapered closed end, internal cylindrical trap element, horizontal outlet, threadless leak-proof couplings, and a sealable drain opening.
counterfactuals.output: A bottle trap for connection to a plumbing fixture includes a housing having an inlet, a substantially horizontal outlet, and a tapered closed lower end. An internal generally cylindrical trap element extends within the housing and cooperates with the housing to define a fluid flow path that maintains a liquid seal between the inlet and outlet. The inlet and outlet are connectable to associated plumbing conduits by threadless, leak-proof couplings configured for push-fit, compression, or sealed engagement. A drain opening formed adjacent the tapered lower end permits removal of accumulated liquid and debris and is selectively closed by a removable sealing member. The tapered lower end directs sediment toward the drain opening, facilitating cleaning without disassembly of the bottle trap.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an improved plumbing bottle trap in formal patent language, including its main body, tailpiece connection, internal trap element, perpendicular outlet orifice, and drain pipe coupling.
counterfactuals.output:
An improved plumbing bottle trap comprises a generally hollow main body defining an internal chamber and having an upper inlet portion, a lower collection portion, and a laterally directed outlet portion. The upper inlet portion includes a tailpiece connection configured to receive and sealingly engage a sink or basin tailpiece, the connection preferably including a compression nut and annular sealing member permitting axial adjustment of the tailpiece relative to the main body.

An internal trap element is disposed within the internal chamber and extends downwardly from the upper inlet portion toward the lower collection portion. The trap element defines an inlet flow passage terminating below a normal retained-liquid level within the chamber, thereby establishing a liquid seal between the inlet flow passage and the outlet portion. The lower collection portion is preferably removable from the main body to facilitate removal of sediment and access to the internal trap element.

The outlet portion defines an outlet orifice having a central axis oriented substantially perpendicular to a longitudinal axis of the tailpiece connection and the internal trap element. The outlet orifice communicates with an upper region of the internal chamber above the lower end of the trap element, such that wastewater flows downwardly through the trap element, around the submerged lower end thereof, and upwardly toward the outlet orifice while a quantity of liquid remains within the chamber to maintain the seal.

A drain pipe coupling is provided at the outlet portion for sealingly connecting the outlet orifice to a downstream drain pipe. The drain pipe coupling may comprise a threaded coupling nut, compression ring, and resilient sealing gasket configured to accommodate limited axial and angular adjustment of the drain pipe. The foregoing arrangement provides a compact, serviceable bottle trap having an adjustable inlet connection, an effective internal liquid seal, and a substantially perpendicular outlet connection suitable for installation in confined plumbing spaces.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise “Disclosed is…” invention summary for a bottle trap whose tapered bottom has an inclined face with a sealable drain orifice.
counterfactuals.output: Disclosed is a bottle trap comprising a trap body having an inlet, an outlet, and a tapered bottom terminating in an inclined face. The inclined face includes a drain orifice selectively closed by a removable seal, enabling convenient drainage and cleaning of the trap.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Prepare a patent abstract for a threadless bottle trap that connects leak-proof to a vertical tailpiece and horizontal drain pipe, with an internal cylindrical element extending at least halfway into the body.
counterfactuals.output: A threadless bottle trap for connecting a substantially vertical tailpiece to a substantially horizontal drain pipe includes a trap body defining an internal chamber, an upper inlet, and a lateral outlet. Threadless sealing assemblies at the inlet and outlet receive the tailpiece and drain pipe, respectively, and include compressible sealing members retained by releasable locking components to form leak-resistant connections without threaded engagement of the pipes. An internal cylindrical element is positioned within the chamber in fluid communication with the inlet and extends axially into the trap body by a distance equal to at least one-half of the body’s internal height. The cylindrical element directs incoming wastewater below a retained liquid level, thereby establishing a water seal between the inlet and outlet. The trap body may include a removable lower portion to permit cleaning and removal of accumulated debris while the tailpiece and drain pipe remain connected.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into one technical paragraph: a bottle-shaped plumbing trap with a tapered closed end, perpendicular side outlet, push-fit couplings, and a drain plug located on an angled bottom face.
counterfactuals.output: A bottle-shaped plumbing trap comprises an elongated chamber having an inlet at a first end, a tapered closed portion at an opposing end, and an outlet extending substantially perpendicular to the chamber’s longitudinal axis. The inlet and outlet incorporate push-fit couplings configured to form fluid-tight connections with adjoining pipes without threaded fasteners or adhesives. The tapered closed portion terminates in an angled bottom face that directs sediment and retained liquid toward a low point, where a removable drain plug is positioned to permit draining, cleaning, and maintenance of the trap.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
